statusDefinitions.methodImplemented: A public client method exists for this operation.
statusDefinitions.typeCoverage: complete means common request and response options have dedicated exported types; partial means a generic record or escape hatch remains.
statusDefinitions.unitTests: present means at least one unit test covers the method or shared transport path; it does not mean every action is covered.
statusDefinitions.integrationTests: tested means the exact operation behavior has passed an integration test on every pinned Solr version listed as tested; partial means some versions or behavior are tested; not-run means no real Solr server test has been executed for the operation.

Unit tests assert the single-document, document-array, and command-map JSON endpoint selection, typed response header, and HTTP error propagation. Unit tests assert single-document, document-array, and command-map endpoint selection, typed response headers, and HTTP error propagation.
Field-specific atomic update modifiers are covered by unit/type assertions and integration tests on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

SolrCloud CREATE/LIST/DELETE, alias lifecycle, implicit-router shard lifecycle, named ADDREPLICA/DELETEREPLICA lifecycle, replica property add/delete and BALANCESHARDUNIQUE responses, plus multi-node MOVEREPLICA and REBALANCELEADERS leader reassignment are tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #177, #192, #209, and PR #142 CI #224). MOVEREPLICA verifies the named replica becomes active on a different live node. REBALANCELEADERS assigns preferredLeader to an active non-leader and verifies it becomes shard leader. Snapshot, backup, and cluster-state response models remain unverified. Additional operation evidence: Typed SolrCloud collection backup/restore actions and asynchronous REQUESTSTATUS/DELETESTATUS tracking. Full backup, list, restore, query read-back, and delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 with a shared local filesystem volume mounted on both SolrCloud nodes. S3 and other external repositories are not certified. LISTALIASES defaults to SolrCollectionAliasesResponse; CREATEALIAS/DELETEALIAS default to SolrCollectionAliasResponse; CLUSTERSTATUS defaults to SolrClusterStatusResponse with extensible collection/shard/replica models. Filtered cluster status and unobserved version-specific fields remain optional/open. CREATESHARD/DELETESHARD now default to SolrCollectionShardOperationResponse and remain integration-tested on all pinned versions. SPLITSHARD has a typed V1 split.key contract (shard or routing-key mode). MIGRATE uses V1 collection/split.key/target.collection/forward.timeout/async parameters and the same response envelope. Both now have opt-in asynchronous integration checks that require SOLR_DESTRUCTIVE_OPT_IN=true, a loopback endpoint, SOLR_CLOUD=true, SOLR_MULTINODE=true, and disposable collections; the manual workflow provisions its own two-node cluster. The tests verify child-shard state and document read-back after split, and target document read-back after migration. The opt-in workflow has not yet been executed, so both operations remain runtime-unverified. Abort, partial-failure recovery, and concurrent-write behavior are not certified. RELOAD now has exact action-specific serialization and isolated collection integration coverage on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. MODIFYCOLLECTION, ADDROLE, and REMOVEROLE now have dedicated serialization and consumer type fixtures; MODIFYCOLLECTION remains runtime-unverified because it mutates collection policy, while role actions remain runtime-unverified because they mutate cluster-wide node role assignments. Named response contracts now cover every action literal: LIST uses SolrCollectionListResponse; CREATE/DELETE/RELOAD/MODIFYCOLLECTION use SolrCollectionAdminResponse; replica lifecycle, movement, balancing, and property actions use SolrCollectionReplicaResponse; ADDROLE/REMOVEROLE use SolrCollectionRoleResponse. CollectionAdminResponse<A> selects the default contract from the action literal while explicit caller generics remain supported. These are extensible response envelopes, not a claim that all action-specific payload fields or all actions are runtime-certified.

Hard commit with waitSearcher is exercised by the CRUD and update integration tests on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests. SolrCommitOptions expose waitSearcher, softCommit, expungeDeletes (hard-commit only), and openSearcher (request parameter); integration tests cover openSearcher=false and expungeDeletes on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Legacy CommitOptions.maxSegments is deprecated and rejected. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.

Config API set-user-property plus GET /config/overlay userProps read-back pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup unsets the property (CI #166). An isolated temporary request handler is added, read back through GET /config, and removed on all three pinned versions. Common set-property/unset-property names and property-specific values are exported for the shared Solr 8.11/9.11/10.1 baseline. SolrConfigRequestHandlerParams adds value-aware autocomplete for common request defaults/appends/invariants (q, fq, fl, rows, start, sort, wt, echoParams, time limits) while keeping the parameter map open. Effective read models distinguish request handlers, search components, response writers, init params, and listeners; response writers expose contentType/charset and listeners expose standard event names while allowing plugin event strings. Search-component and other plugin-defined options remain open and use customOptions for flattened command-specific extensions. Consumer fixtures cover typed common handler parameters, invalid known values, named read models, existing set-property allow-list, user properties, and config responses. Security API authentication/authorization checks remain in the separate security matrix (CI #162); version-specific common properties remain outside the shared property union.

STATUS has exported CoreAdminStatusResponse with typed per-core paths/config metadata, optional index statistics, initialization failures, and extensible unknown fields. Non-STATUS actions default to exported CoreAdminCommandResponse (responseHeader plus extensible fields); callers can supply a more specific generic. Unit and consumer type fixtures cover minimal/detailed STATUS payloads and non-STATUS response inference. Isolated CREATE, STATUS, and RELOAD pass with unique disposable cores on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup UNLOADs them (CI #145). RENAME, SWAP, MERGEINDEXES, SPLIT, REQUESTSTATUS, and REQUESTRECOVERY are not runtime-certified.

Typed SolrExportParams requires fl and sort, supports filter query arrays, raw or structured sort expressions, batchSize, response writer selection, optional local expr, and customParams. export() returns the raw backpressure-aware Response. Sort fields must be single-valued docValues int/long/float/double/string fields; fl additionally supports date/boolean and multi-valued fields. includeStoredFields is documented for Solr 10.1 but remains version-specific. Existing live raw-response integration test covers Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0; unit tests cover typed serialization.
Reads the effective configuration through GET /config. The method has dedicated request serialization and integration evidence.
Reads the persisted Config API overlay through GET /config/overlay. Kept separate from getConfig because the endpoint and semantics differ.

JVM response-format coverage remains distinct: observed JSON registry on Solr 8/9 and Prometheus exposition on Solr 10.1. A node group check asserts non-empty JSON registry data on Solr 8/9 and Prometheus samples on Solr 10.1. Registry, prefix, and regex filters are asserted against JSON responses on Solr 8/9; Solr 10.1 supports Prometheus/OpenMetrics rather than the JSON writer. Exported SolrMetricsJsonResponse, SolrMetricsRegistry, and SolrMetricValue model stable envelope/value shapes while leaving registry and metric names open for plugins and future Solr versions.

Optimize followed by query asserting committed documents remain available passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments and waitSearcher with unit and consumer type coverage; the existing optimize behavior remains integration-tested on all pinned versions. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments, waitSearcher, and openSearcher; maxSegments is optimize-only and defaults to Solr's unlimited target. The integration test exercises maxSegments on all pinned versions. openSearcher is request-parameter serialized; its optimize-specific runtime effect remains unverified. Ping response status OK is asserted on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145).

Generic SolrResponse<TDocument> and SolrQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> types expose document metadata, classic facet counts, caller-shaped JSON facets, highlighting, grouping, stats, and debug sections. Consumer compile tests verify document inference and response-section property types. Basic query serialization and document retrieval plus cursorMark multi-page traversal are tested on the pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; typed declarations do not certify every optional response section at runtime. Typed classic Facet Component options cover field facets and per-field limit/offset/sort/mincount/missing/prefix/method overrides, query facets, and numeric/date range facets with include/other/hardend and filter/dv methods. Solr date bucketing uses range facets; legacy facet.date parameters were removed in Solr 6. Integration coverage asserts field/query counts and numeric/date range response sections on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed highlighting options cover field selection, highlighter method, snippet/fragment sizing, field matching, alternate fields, phrase and multi-term highlighting, encoders/tags, and per-field overrides. Unit and consumer type tests cover parameter serialization and invalid values; integration tests verify returned snippets on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed Result Grouping options cover group.field, group.func, group.query, per-group limit/offset/sort, group format/main/ngroups/truncate/facet/cache settings; typed grouped response models expose matches, group counts, and per-group document lists. Typed collapse and expand options serialize the Collapsing Query Parser filter and Expand component parameters, with expanded document maps in the response. Standalone integration tests verify field grouping, group sorting, collapse selection, and expansion on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Function grouping and collapse remain subject to Solr's documented distributed/shard-local limitations. Typed Stats Component options support repeated fields, per-field local statistic selection, percentiles, cardinality, tag/key/excludeTags, global stats facets, and calcDistinct. SolrFieldStats response models include nested facet breakdowns, percentiles, and cardinality. Unit and consumer type tests cover encoding and response properties; integration tests verify numeric aggregates, distinct values/counts, cardinality, and category breakdowns on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed MoreLikeThis Search Component options cover field selection, result count, term/document-frequency thresholds, word/token/query-term limits, boosting, query fields, and interesting terms. Unit and consumer type tests cover serialization and response typing; integration tests verify similar-document results on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Geospatial geofilt/bbox filters and geodist sorting are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 using an isolated LatLonPointSpatialField and deterministic nearby/far points; assertions verify inclusion/exclusion and nearest-to-farthest ordering.

JSON Request API query body now has a typed SolrJsonQueryRequest model and recursive JSON Facet API terms/query/range definitions, nested metrics, and domain transformations. SolrJsonQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> exposes caller-typed facet results. Unit and consumer type tests cover nested serialization and invalid discriminators; integration tests verify terms/query/range facets, nested metrics, and excludeTags domain behavior on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Other JSON Request API options remain available through params or the legacy custom-body overload.

Typed V1 ReplicationHandler commands for enablereplication, disablereplication, indexversion, fetchindex, abortfetch, snappull, abort, enablepoll, disablepoll, details, filelist, backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup; replicationFile() returns raw filecontent streams. Live integration coverage on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 covers indexversion, details, filelist, and filecontent. enablereplication/disablereplication are integration-tested on a configured leader; fetchindex/abortfetch (Solr 10), snappull/abort (Solr 8/9), enablepoll, and disablepoll have unit serialization coverage, but a multi-core leader/follower fetch cycle is not yet certified. Core-level backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are integration-tested on all three pinned versions. Filelist uses the generation returned by newer Solr indexversion responses and falls back to the legacy indexversion parameter when that field is absent. Additional operation evidence: Core-level ReplicationHandler backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are typed. Backup defaults to the core dataDir; restore status is polled with restorestatus. Full backup/restore/read-back/delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Custom filesystem locations must be permitted by server allowPaths.
Returns raw replication file content as a Response stream; distinct from command-based replication operations.

Generic escape hatch. It does not imply typed support for every Solr endpoint. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction.

Generic raw-response escape hatch using the shared Solr transport. Supports typed methods, query parameters, headers, request bodies, cancellation, timeouts, retry policy, configured validation, and standard Solr error classes. Relative paths and same-origin absolute URLs are supported; cross-origin absolute URLs, embedded credentials, and fragments are rejected before Fetch to prevent credential leakage. String bodies are passed through unchanged when callers supply an explicit Content-Type. Custom endpoint behavior is unverified on Solr 8/9/10 until endpoint-specific integration tests are added. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction.

Field, field-type, dynamic-field add/replace/delete and copy-field add/delete commands are unit-tested for exact serialization and integration-tested with responseHeader.status plus schema read-back on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Copy-field replacement is implemented by delete+add because Solr has no native replace-copy-field command. Integration tests verify full schema metadata, name, version, uniqueKey, and similarity response envelopes on all pinned versions. Similarity plugin mutation remains runtime-unverified. The public client implements V1 Schema API routes; Solr 10 V2 routes are not included.

Authentication overloads default to SolrAuthenticationResponse and accept SolrAuthenticationCommand for BasicAuthPlugin set-user, delete-user, and set-property operations, including documented MultiAuthPlugin Basic scheme wrappers for set-user/set-property. BasicAuth configuration exposes hashed credential strings; these must not be logged or treated as plaintext. Authorization has separate SolrAuthorizationResponse/SolrAuthorizationCommand types for RuleBasedAuthorizationPlugin. Custom plugin schemas remain open/unsupported beyond the explicit extension points. Unit serialization and compile-time fixtures cover auth command shapes; existing authenticated read and set-property/read-back integration tests pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. User create/delete mutations are not performed against shared integration security state.

Default SolrStreamingExpressionResponse models the JSON result-set envelope and extensible tuple fields; SolrStreamingExpressionErrorTuple describes in-band EXCEPTION tuples. Callers can supply a response or tuple-specific generic shape. Unknown envelope and tuple fields remain accessible. HTTP-level Solr errors continue through the shared typed transport. SolrCloud search is integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Unit tests cover response parsing, in-band error tuples, cancellation during body consumption, and cleanup after body-stream errors. This API parses the complete JSON response and is not an incremental tuple-stream parser.
